quarterly_data.signal: Broadscale setback: in Q2 the company completed testing and determined that its assay configuration changes did not sufficiently improve probe candidate performance to support a 2027 general availability of the broadscale application at target specifications. Chief Scientist: remaining work is increasing probe library diversity through affinity maturation (an inherently long lead time activity), improving the machine learning layer and stabilizing the new assay architecture with partners; management is not putting a new timeline on broadscale and says the underlying science is sound.
quarterly_data.figure: no 2027 broadscale general availability; no new timeline

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: the company is effectively tripling the number of people focused on proteoform development while reducing the broadscale team by roughly half; application-specific R&D, previously weighted heavily towards broadscale, is now roughly two-thirds proteoforms and one-third broadscale, all within the planned spend envelope.
quarterly_data.figure: proteoform headcount effectively tripling; broadscale team cut by roughly half; ~two-thirds proteoforms / one-third broadscale

quarterly_data.signal: Chief Scientist: in Q2 the oncology work was narrowed to three candidates, AKT1, EGFR and p53, developed in parallel; all three cleared the company's reproducibility and accuracy criteria and moved into development, with AKT1 furthest along and expected to be first to market. The tau assay took about five years to build while the first oncology markers reached the same technical bar in about a year; management says proteoform development is now bottlenecked by capacity, not scientific uncertainty, and expects new assays at a cadence measured in months.
quarterly_data.figure: AKT1, EGFR and p53 cleared reproducibility and accuracy criteria; tau ~5 years vs oncology ~1 year

quarterly_data.signal: Roadmap additions: a third oncology proteoform assay and additional kits are expected to reach general availability in late 2027; the company expects a roughly 100-fold reduction in required sample input in early 2027 and cerebrospinal fluid support for the tau assay in 2028, with oncology biofluid support expected earlier; new content and capabilities are expected roughly every six months; a Voyager beta unit placement remains on track for this year.
quarterly_data.figure: third oncology assay GA late 2027; ~100-fold lower sample input early 2027; tau CSF 2028; beta unit in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Chief Scientist: data from the company's alpha instrument at the Buck Institute showed a median CV of roughly 5.5% against an industry norm closer to 25%, showed that different APOE genetic risk variants carry distinct tau proteoform signatures, and found that model systems widely used in Alzheimer's research show markedly different tau proteoform landscapes from one another. CEO: the company signed a collaboration with the Allen Institute for Brain Science covers analysis of human brain samples across brain regions, genetic backgrounds and disease severities.

Q2 revenue came mostly from grant revenue for the Michael J. Fox Foundation-funded alpha-synuclein (Parkinson's) proteoform assay development, with the remainder service revenue from the first Early Access Program project, with Baylor College of Medicine, the first early access customer for the tau assay. CFO expects fairly steady Michael J. Fox Foundation grant revenue through 2026 and into 2027, although the amounts might vary by quarter, and does not expect additional early access customers to be a major revenue driver this year.

Q2 2026 operating expenses were $15.9 million, down approximately 7% year on year (R&D $9.6 million, SG&A $6.3 million); net loss was $14.5 million, or $0.11 per share, versus $15 million a year earlier; cash usage was approximately $14.2 million in the quarter. CFO now expects full-year operating expenses below prior guidance, representing year-over-year growth of less than 10%.
quarterly_data.figure: opex $15.9M (-7%); net loss $14.5M; FY opex growth less than 10%, below prior guidance

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the tau assay supports only brain tissue, and roughly 9 out of 10 sales conversations ask for cerebrospinal fluid or blood support; because tissue samples are common in oncology, management sees the near-term serviceable opportunity in oncology at five to ten times that of neurodegeneration and calls AKT1 a significant unlock; if AKT1 early access comes this year and into the beginning of next year, he thinks the oncology business will start to ramp significantly faster than neurodegeneration.
quarterly_data.figure: oncology 5-10x neurodegeneration serviceable opportunity; ~9 of 10 conversations ask for CSF or blood

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: proteoform measurements may translate directly into clinical research and eventually diagnostics, so the company could be pulled into the clinical market earlier than planned, and it expects opportunities to partner with pharma on new targets, AI-model data sets and bespoke assays; both are described as early, with no plan or timeline.
